units.translation: maddened – a maenad of Hera, driven by goading pains
Let insatiable faction raise a cry over the stoning sacrifice for the race
This smells of sacrifices at the hearth
But now in darkness it roars, causing pain to the heart
altars receiving elders, abounding with garlands
the best and most pleasing of these things
Being a prophet in my heart, I advised you these things kindly
Thus A. I. Ahrensius for μυθοῦσθαι [to speak].
But I, for I pity, will not be angry
to be angry about these things
as being in doubt whether to be angry with the city
not to be angry with the gods in misfortunes
Let not heart-filling, spear-mad ruin carry you off
and do not waste away your swelling heart by force
nourishing the heart with torches in festivities
cast my words into your heart
for the iron-hearted spirit, blazing with courage, breathed
neither in form nor in spirit nor in bearing of arms blameworthy
the heart, too prophetic, is greatly troubled within
for his wits steered his heart
crying out great Ares from their hearts
the heart within, self-taught, sings the dirge of the Erinys
so he rouses his own heart as he falls
the heart is insatiate from its mother
painful things that greatly stir the heart
they shook their hearts with pale fear
I have a heart that knows horses

corrupt reading, which the scholiast explains as ἥτις ἐστὶ θυμοβόρος λύπη τῆς φρενός [which is a heart-eating pain of the mind]. The sense suits καινοῦ θυμοφθόρου | ἄλγους [of a new heart-destroying grief], which I proposed in Philologus vol. 18 p. 66. Weil conjectured λύπης, θυμοφθόρον ἄτην [of pain, a heart-destroying ruin].
which is a heart-eating pain of the mind
in the words of Minerva to the chorus of Furies

Schol. ὀργαῖς [angers]. Because even those drunk with wine (rather not drunk with wine) become in some way mad. Hermann: “ἄοινα θυμώματα [wineless angers] are angers not born from wine and heavier and more lasting than those of the drunk. The opinion of those who think that the quarrels inflicted by the Furies are called wineless angers because their sacrifices were wineless is foolish.”
But do not cast into my house bloody whetstones, harm to young entrails, mad with wineless angers
angers. Because even those drunk with wine
not drunk with wine) become in some way mad
like tunny fish or some catch of fish
casting his left eye like a tunny fish
who endured without groaning like a tunny fish
incense before children and the marriage rite
